speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the number of Polytechnic graduates who dropped out from the SGUnited Traineeships Programme; and (b) what are the reasons for the drop-outs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Singapore Business Federation (SBF), our programme partner managing the SGUnited Traineeships Programme, surveys host organisations and trainees who have completed the programme, or left halfway.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The SGUnited Traineeships Programme provides meaningful opportunities to graduates to pick up skills in preparation for full-time jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: I am encouraged to see that the majority of trainees continue to go through with their traineeships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For participants who need career assistance, they can approach Workforce Singapore (WSG) or NTUC’s e2i through physical touchpoints such as the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres, WSG’s Careers Connect and its mobile extension, Careers Connect On-the-Go, as well as NTUC-e2i’s career centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They may also visit the MyCareersFuture portal to search for job opportunities that suit their skills and competencies.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Is that the reason why most of them got jobs or stayed on in the programme?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the order of the day.
